name: LT8391EFE#PBF
title: 60V four-switch synchronous buck-boost LED controller, spread spectrum
summary: The LT8391 controls four external N-channel MOSFETs around a single inductor to regulate LED current with the input above, below or equal to the output, from 4V to 60V in and 0V to 60V out. Peak-buck/peak-boost current mode gives smooth region changes, at a fixed 150kHz to 650kHz, an external clock, or ±15% triangle spread spectrum. LED current is set by a sense resistor and two CTRL inputs (20:1 analog dimming, ±3% at 100mV full scale) and dimmed by external (up to 2000:1) or internal (up to 128:1) PWM through a high-side PMOS driver. Open and short LED faults are flagged on FAULT, with hiccup, latch-off or keep-running response.
key_figures: 0V to 60V (51V LED string with open-LED protection)
±3% (97 mV to 103 mV at 100 mV full scale)

notes: E, I and H are the temperature grades (Note 2); the grade is shown on a label on the shipping container. Some packages come in 500-unit reels with the #TRMPBF suffix.

pins.name: BG1
pins.function: Gate drive for the buck-side bottom N-channel MOSFET (switch B); swings from ground to INTVCC.

pins.name: BST1
pins.function: Floating supply for the buck-side top gate driver. An internal Schottky diode from INTVCC charges it; a bootstrap capacitor goes from BST1 to SW1. Swings from one diode drop below INTVCC up to VIN + INTVCC.

pins.name: SW1
pins.function: Buck-side switch node; moves between a Schottky drop below ground and VIN.

pins.name: TG1
pins.function: Gate drive for the buck-side top N-channel MOSFET (switch A); swings from SW1 to BST1.

pins.name: LSP
pins.function: Positive side of the inductor current sense resistor RSENSE. Use a Kelvin connection.

pins.name: LSN
pins.function: Negative side of the inductor current sense resistor RSENSE. Use a Kelvin connection.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input. Also tells the controller the input voltage for picking the buck, buck-boost or boost region. Bypass to ground close by with at least 1µF ceramic.

pins.name: INTVCC
pins.function: Output of the internal 5V linear regulator fed from VIN; it runs the control circuits and gate drivers. Bypass to ground close by with at least 4.7µF ceramic.

pins.name: EN/UVLO
pins.function: Enable and undervoltage lockout. Below 0.3V the part is shut down and VIN draws under 2µA; above 1.227V it runs. A divider from VIN uses the 1.214V falling threshold to set an input UVLO, and the 2.5µA pull-down current sets its hysteresis. Tie to VIN when neither is wanted.

pins.name: RP
pins.function: Sets the internal PWM dimming frequency with a resistor to ground. Do not leave open and do not use more than 1MΩ. Ground it when an external PWM signal drives the PWM pin.

pins.name: PWM
pins.function: PWM dimming input. External dimming: a digital pulse from 0V to above 1.5V, with RP grounded. Internal dimming: an analog level between 1V and 2V compared with an internal ramp. Tie to INTVCC when dimming is not used. Holding it low turns TG1 and TG2 off, BG1 and BG2 on, cuts VC off from its internal loads and turns PWMTG off.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: Accurate 2V reference able to source 1mA. Bypass to ground close by with a 0.47µF ceramic capacitor.

pins.name: CTRL1
pins.function: Sets the LED current sense threshold: 0mV to 90mV linearly for 0.25V to 1.15V, a smooth bend between 1.15V and 1.35V, and the 100mV full scale above 1.35V. Driven by a reference or a divider from VREF; tie to VREF for full scale. Below 0.2V switching stops.

pins.name: ISP
pins.function: Positive side of the LED current sense resistor RLED. Use a Kelvin connection.

pins.name: ISN
pins.function: Negative side of the LED current sense resistor RLED. Use a Kelvin connection.

pins.name: CTRL2
pins.function: Second current sense threshold input, meant for derating LED current with temperature through a divider from VREF that has a negative temperature coefficient. Same transfer as CTRL1 (0mV to 90mV over 0.25V to 1.15V, 100mV above 1.35V). Tie to VREF for full scale; below 0.2V switching stops.

pins.name: FAULT
pins.function: LED fault flag, active low; needs an external pull-up. Pulled low for an open LED (VFB > 0.95V and V(ISP-ISN) < 10mV) or a short LED (VFB < 0.25V). The flag is updated only while PWM is high and held while PWM is low.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start timer: a capacitor to ground, charged by an internal 12.5µA current, ramps the FB regulation level; 0.1µF is the suggested value. UVLO or thermal shutdown pulls SS to ground at once and stops switching. One resistor from SS to VREF picks the LED fault mode: none for hiccup, 499k for latch-off, 100k for keep-running.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Voltage feedback for constant-voltage regulation (regulated to 1.00V) and LED fault detection. Open or short LED pulls FAULT low and enters the selected fault mode; overvoltage (VFB > 1.05V) turns off TG1, BG1, TG2, BG2 and PWMTG.

pins.name: VC
pins.function: Error amplifier output that sets the inductor current comparator threshold; an RC network to ground compensates the loop. While PWM is low the pin is disconnected from internal loads so it holds its voltage.

pins.name: RT
pins.function: Resistor to ground sets the internal oscillator between 150kHz and 650kHz.

pins.name: SYNC/SPRD
pins.function: Ground for the internal oscillator frequency; drive with a clock to synchronize; tie to INTVCC for ±15% triangle spread spectrum around the internal frequency.

pins.name: PWMTG
pins.function: Drive for an external high-side PMOS PWM switch: a buffered, inverted copy of PWM swinging from VOUT down to the higher of (VOUT – 5V) and 1.2V. Leave open if unused.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Output voltage sense, used for region selection, and the positive rail of the PWMTG driver. Bypass to ground close by with at least 1µF ceramic.

pins.name: TG2
pins.function: Gate drive for the boost-side top N-channel MOSFET (switch D); swings from SW2 to BST2.

pins.name: SW2
pins.function: Boost-side switch node; moves between a Schottky drop below ground and VOUT.

pins.name: BST2
pins.function: Floating supply for the boost-side top gate driver, charged from INTVCC through an internal Schottky diode; a bootstrap capacitor goes from BST2 to SW2. Swings from one diode drop below INTVCC up to VOUT + INTVCC.

pins.name: BG2
pins.function: Gate drive for the boost-side bottom N-channel MOSFET (switch C); swings from ground to INTVCC.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground, the exposed pad. Solder it straight to the ground plane.

rows: FB, PWM, SYNC/SPRD, CTRL1, CTRL2, FAULT
notes: Note 1: Going past these limits can damage the part for good; sitting at any one of them for long stretches can shorten its life and lower its reliability.

Note 2: The E grade is tested to its specifications from 0°C to 125°C junction; over –40°C to 125°C it is held to them by design, characterization and statistical process control. The I grade is guaranteed over –40°C to 125°C and the H grade over –40°C to 150°C junction. Lifetime falls at high junction temperature and is derated above 125°C.

Note 3: An overtemperature shutdown guards against brief overloads; while it is active the junction is above 150°C. Running continuously above the maximum operating junction temperature can harm reliability.

circuits.title: 98% efficient 50W (25V, 2A) buck-boost LED driver
circuits.description: A 6V to 55V supply drives a 25V, 2A LED string through four N-channel switches around one 10µH inductor. The 0.004Ω resistor between SW1 and the inductor gives the controller its inductor current; the 0.05Ω resistor in the output path sets 2A at the 100mV full-scale threshold, with CTRL2 tied to VREF and CTRL1 pulled up to VREF and open to an analog dimming signal. The 1M/34.8k divider on FB sets the open-LED output limit. A PMOS driven by PWMTG disconnects the string while PWM DIM is low. RT = 100k sets 400kHz; RP and SYNC/SPRD are grounded, so the part runs from its own oscillator and dims from the external PWM signal. 499k/221k on EN/UVLO set the input undervoltage lockout.

circuits.title: 98% efficient 50W (25V 2A) buck-boost LED driver
circuits.description: The 50W typical-application driver with every option brought out. A switch on RP either grounds it for external PWM dimming or leaves the 200k resistor for 195Hz internal dimming, set by a 100k potentiometer from VREF on the PWM pin. A second switch puts SYNC/SPRD on an external clock, ground (fixed 400kHz) or INTVCC (spread spectrum). 1µF capacitors bypass the VIN and VOUT pins, and an optional Schottky diode goes from LED+ to ground.

circuits.title: 95% efficient 12W (12V 1A) buck-boost LED driver with dual package MOSFETs
circuits.description: A 12V, 1A version of the same driver from a 5V to 56V input. Each side of the bridge uses one dual MOSFET package: M1 holds switches A and B, M2 holds switches D and C. RSENSE is 0.015Ω, RLED 0.1Ω (1A at 100mV), and 1M/75k on FB sets the output limit. A Si2307DS PMOS on PWMTG does the dimming disconnect; compensation is 2.0k with 4.7nF.

circuits.title: 93% efficient 84W buck-boost LED driver from 24VAC
circuits.description: 24VAC at 60Hz feeds a bridge of four N-channel MOSFETs driven by an LT4320, giving a rail PVIN that pulses at 120Hz with 1µF capacitors on it. The LT8391 runs from PVIN at 500kHz (RT = 75.0k). CTRL1 takes a 1M/37.4k divider from PVIN; the LED string (15V to 25V) carries 0A to 6A pulsing at 120Hz, and the input power factor is 98%. PWM is tied to INTVCC, PWMTG is unconnected, and 100k from SS to VREF selects keep-running fault mode.

circuits.title: 97% efficient 8A buck-boost SLA battery charger
circuits.description: The controller charges a sealed lead-acid battery from an 8V to 60V input. A 0.012Ω resistor, with two 10Ω resistors and 2.2µF between it and ISP/ISN, senses the 7.8A charge current; CTRL1 sits on a 10k/15k divider from VREF. FB takes a 100k/7.87k divider from the output, plus a second 100k to ground through M5, whose gate is on the active-low C/10 flag (FAULT, pulled up by 10k). Charge voltage is 14.6V and float voltage 13.6V. CTRL2 is pulled to VREF by 10k and brought out as a current-adjust input. PWM is tied to INTVCC, RP is grounded, 174k sets 250kHz and 100k from SS to VREF selects keep-running mode.

operation.text: Four external N-channel switches and one inductor form a buck-boost stage: A from VIN to SW1, B from SW1 to ground, C from SW2 to ground and D from SW2 to VOUT, with the inductor and RSENSE in series between SW1 and SW2. RSENSE, read at LSP and LSN, serves both peak current control and reverse current detection in all three regions. The controller chooses one of four states from the VIN/VOUT ratio, with hysteresis at every boundary: peak-buck control in the buck region, peak-buck in the buck-boost region, peak-boost in the buck-boost region, and peak-boost in the boost region.

Peak-buck control hands over to peak-boost at a VIN/VOUT ratio of 0.98 and returns at 1.02. Boost operation extends up to a ratio of 0.75 to 0.85 (enter buck-boost at 0.85 rising, back to boost at 0.75 falling); buck operation starts above 1.18 to 1.33 (enter buck at 1.33 rising, back to buck-boost at 1.18 falling).

operation.topic: Buck region (VIN much higher than VOUT)
operation.text: D stays on and C stays off. Each cycle A turns on; when the inductor current reaches the peak level set by VC at comparator A3, A turns off and B conducts for the rest of the cycle, as in a synchronous buck.

operation.topic: Buck-boost region, peak-buck (VIN a little above VOUT)
operation.text: Each cycle starts with A and C on. C turns off after 15% of the cycle and D conducts for the remaining 85%. When the inductor current reaches the peak-buck level during A+D, A turns off and B turns on until the cycle ends.

operation.topic: Buck-boost region, peak-boost (VIN a little below VOUT)
operation.text: A is on for the first 85% of the cycle and B for the last 15%. Each cycle starts with A and C on; when the inductor current reaches the peak-boost level set by VC at comparator A4, C turns off and D turns on. After 85% of the cycle A gives way to B.

operation.topic: Boost region (VIN much lower than VOUT)
operation.text: A stays on and B stays off. Each cycle C turns on; at the peak-boost current C turns off and D conducts until the cycle ends, as in a synchronous boost.

The control is fixed-frequency current mode. Amplifier A1 amplifies the RSENSE voltage and adds an oscillator slope-compensation ramp; the sum goes to the buck and boost comparators, whose thresholds come from VC. VC is the diode-OR of EA1, which holds FB at 1V, and EA2, which holds V(ISP-ISN) at the level set by CTRL1 or CTRL2. The two amplifiers are gain-matched so the hand-over between constant voltage and constant current is smooth on one compensation network.

Both reverse current thresholds sit at –4mV, so a little energy returns from output to input each cycle and the part normally keeps full switching frequency in CCM or DCM; this keeps pulse skipping from dropping below 100Hz, which would make the LEDs flicker. In the buck region B turns off when the buck reverse threshold trips during B+D; in the boost region D turns off when the boost threshold trips during A+D; in buck-boost D turns off on the boost threshold in A+D and both B and D turn off on the buck threshold in B+D. With a small inductor and large ripple the part can skip pulses for several cycles.

Each top driver runs from its bootstrap capacitor, recharged from INTVCC through internal diode D1 or D2 while its top switch is off. When the part stays in the buck or boost region one top switch never turns off, so an internal path keeps that capacitor at 4.6V: BST1 is fed from VOUT and BST2, and BST2 is fed from VIN and BST1. Buck and boost operation therefore need no periodic top-switch refresh, and make none of its noise.

Below the 0.3V minimum shutdown threshold on EN/UVLO the part draws under 2µA. Above 1V maximum it starts its bandgap and the INTVCC regulator and sits in UVLO, sinking 2.5µA into EN/UVLO. Once INTVCC is above its 3.78V typical rising threshold, EN/UVLO is above 1.227V typical and the junction is below the 165°C typical thermal shutdown, the hysteresis current switches off and VREF starts charging. Power-on reset lasts until VREF passes its 1.89V typical rising threshold; the part then waits for CTRL1, CTRL2 and PWM to allow switching.

In POR the SS pin is held down through 100Ω. SS must fall below 0.2V to enter INIT, where the part waits 10µs for SS to discharge fully. It moves to UP/PRE when PWMON goes high, which needs both CTRL pins above their rising dim-off threshold (0.228V typical) and external or internal PWM on. In UP/PRE 12.5µA charges SS with switching and PWMTG off. Above 0.25V on SS it enters UP/TRY: PWMTG turns on with switching still off, to confirm the output capacitor voltage suits the LED string before any energy is delivered. If excess current trips the ISP/ISN overcurrent comparator (ISOC) the part returns to POR, so it hiccups with SS between 0V and 0.25V and bleeds the output down. After 10µs in UP/TRY without ISOC it enters UP/RUN.

In UP/RUN switching is enabled and, while SS is below 1V, FB is regulated to the SS voltage instead of 1V. The 12.5µA current ramps SS from 0.25V up through 1V so VOUT rises smoothly to the LED string voltage. Above 1.75V on SS the part enters OK/RUN and open and short LED detection becomes active.

Open LED means VFB > 0.95V with V(ISP-ISN) < 10mV; short LED means VFB < 0.25V. Either one pulls FAULT low and moves the part to FAULT/RUN, where 1.25µA discharges SS. Below 1.7V on SS it enters DOWN/STOP: switching stops and detection is off, with the fault held. Below 0.2V, with PWMON still high, it goes back to UP/RUN. A resistor from SS to VREF picks the behaviour: none gives hiccup (SS cycling between 0.2V and 1.75V until the fault clears), 499k gives latch-off until EN/UVLO is toggled low and high, and 100k gives keep-running, where the part keeps regulating the programmed VOUT during an open LED or the current during a short LED.

With small output capacitors VOUT can overshoot well past the regulated level when the LED string opens, since the 1V FB loop is too slow to catch it. When FB reaches 1.05V switching stops (TG1, BG1, TG2, BG2 off) and PWMTG turns off to disconnect the LEDs.
Open-drain, pulled low on an open or short LED. The status is updated only when SS is above 1.75V and PWM is high, and held while PWM is low.

Fixed frequency from 150kHz to 650kHz, set by RT to ground with SYNC/SPRD grounded (Table 1). Lower frequency cuts MOSFET switching loss and suits high power; higher frequency shrinks the inductor and capacitors and suits low power. Noise-sensitive systems may place the frequency to keep switching noise out of a sensitive band.

With SYNC/SPRD tied to INTVCC the frequency is swept in a triangle ±15% around the RT frequency to lower EMI. The internal oscillator is synchronized to the rising edge of PWM in both fixed-frequency and spread spectrum operation, so PWM dimming is flicker-free. Conducted EMI of the 50W typical application was compared with spread spectrum on and off against the CISPR25 average and peak limits over 150kHz to 2000kHz.

A clock on SYNC/SPRD sets the switching frequency through an internal PLL, so the clock need not be near the RT frequency. 50% duty is best; otherwise keep it between 10% and 90%. Each rising edge starts a cycle, turning on A and C or A and D. With an external clock, SYNC and PWM need aligned rising edges for flicker-free PWM dimming.

Higher frequency allows smaller inductance. Pick a low-core-loss inductor such as ferrite, with low DC resistance, rated for the peak current without saturating; a shielded part lowers radiated noise.

The 50mV maximum thresholds in peak-buck and peak-boost are independent of duty cycle and set the peak inductor current in every region. Size RSENSE for both the buck case at VIN(MAX) and the boost case at VIN(MIN) and use the smaller value, with 20% to 30% margin.

Four N-channel MOSFETs are needed, two top (A, D) and two bottom (B, C). Gate drive comes from 5V INTVCC, so they must be logic-level types. Key ratings are VBR(DSS), VGS(TH), RDS(ON), CRSS and IDS(MAX). Because region changes go by the VIN/VOUT ratio, large IR drops in the power path can upset smooth transitions; choose low RDS(ON) and low DCR to meet the path resistance limit. For a given output, the worst case for switch A is buck operation at highest input, and for switch C boost operation at lowest input. For low-Qg MOSFETs a 5.1Ω gate resistor is needed on switch C.

operation.topic: Optional Schottky diodes DB and DD
operation.text: Schottky diodes across B and D carry current in the dead time so the MOSFET body diodes do not turn on and store charge. DB cuts reverse recovery current between B off and A on; DD does the same between D off and C on. They raise efficiency and lower switch stress, and must sit right next to their MOSFET to keep loop inductance low.

Input current is most discontinuous in the buck region and output current in the boost region; both networks need low ESR and enough capacitance. Parallel combinations of tantalum, polymer, aluminium electrolytic and ceramic parts are typical, including low-ESR OS-CON or POSCAP types. Place ceramics of at least 1µF from VIN and VOUT to GND close to the pins. X5R and X7R hold capacitance over voltage and temperature; small 0805 and 0603 ceramics lose much of theirs at working voltage.

An internal P-channel LDO makes 5V at INTVCC from VIN to power the control circuits and gate drivers. It can source 110mA peak and needs at least 4.7µF ceramic to ground. Supply current is mostly gate charge; dissipation is VIN • IINTVCC, so large MOSFETs at high frequency and high VIN can push the junction past its limit. Check input current at maximum VIN in continuous mode.

TG1 and TG2 swing between their SW and BST pins. CBST1 and CBST2 charge to INTVCC through the internal diodes while the matching top switch is off and should hold about 100 times the top-switch gate charge; 0.1µF to 0.47µF X5R or X7R is enough in most designs.

A divider from VIN to EN/UVLO sets the input UVLO. The enable falling threshold is 1.214V with 10mV hysteresis, and the pin sinks 2.5µA below 1.214V, so the top resistor R1 adds hysteresis. An NMOS from EN/UVLO to ground gives run/stop control while keeping UVLO; when on it holds the part in shutdown below 2µA.

RLED in series with the LEDs is Kelvin-sensed at ISP and ISN. Above 1.35V on both CTRL pins the threshold is the full 100mV; either pin can dim the current to zero, with relative accuracy falling as the threshold falls. Do not leave CTRL1 or CTRL2 open; tie an unused one to VREF. A CTRL pin can also take a thermistor divider for LED overtemperature protection, or a divider from VIN to cut power and switch current at low VIN. Some switching-frequency ripple across ISP-ISN is normal and grows with LED current, lower frequency and smaller output capacitance; the VC capacitor averages it. Ripple above 20mV peak-to-peak does not cause misoperation but can offset the average from the programmed value.

Analog dimming adjusts the current through CTRL1 or CTRL2 (20:1 range, ±3% at 100mV full scale); PWM dimming switches the current between zero and full and gives much higher ratios without colour shift. While PWM is low the switch demand is held on VC, shortening recovery when PWM goes high, and a high-side PMOS in the LED path keeps the output capacitor from discharging. The shortest usable PWM on-time depends on frequency, inductance and compensation. External PWM dimming uses RP below 30k and a clock on PWM. Internal PWM dimming uses one of the five RP values of Table 3 to set the dimming frequency and a DC level from 1V to 2V on PWM (a source or a divider from VREF) to set duty from 0% to 100% in 1/128 steps; a 1µF ceramic on PWM limits duty jitter from switching noise.

Recommended in most designs to get the highest dimming ratio and to protect the LEDs during faults; unlike a low-side NMOS it needs only one wire out to the LEDs, returning through the chassis. Its VDS rating needs to be above the FB-programmed open-LED output voltage, |VGS(TH)| should be below 3V, and its ID rating above ILED(MAX).

The VC pin of the transconductance error amplifier carries the compensation. For typical LED designs 10nF on VC is enough; always add a series resistor, which speeds VC slewing and keeps LED current tighter during fast input transients.

Main losses: DC I²R in the MOSFETs, sense resistor, inductor and traces, dominant at high current; transition loss while A or C switches, depending on input voltage, load current, drive strength and MOSFET capacitance; INTVCC current for drivers and control; RMS current in CIN (buck region) and COUT (boost region); and smaller items such as DB and DD conduction, inductor core loss at light load, and reverse recovery from A in buck and C in boost. Input current is the best indicator when tuning efficiency.

Use a dedicated ground plane with no traces, on the layer next to the power MOSFETs; multilayer boards help with heat. Group CIN, A, B and DB in one tight area and COUT, C, D and DD in another, with short loops. Give each power part several large vias to ground and use planes for VIN and VOUT; flood unused areas with copper tied to a DC net. Return small-signal parts to the exposed pad, joined to power ground near the sources of B and C. Keep A and C close to the controller with short power ground, BG and SW traces. Keep SW1, SW2, BST1, BST2, TG1 and TG2 away from sensitive nodes. Join the output and input capacitor negative terminals as closely as possible. Put CBST1 at BST1-SW1 and CBST2 at BST2-SW2, and CIN and COUT close to the MOSFETs. Run LSP and LSN together at minimum spacing away from switch nodes, with their filter capacitor near the IC and Kelvin taps at RSENSE. Put the VC network near the IC to signal ground, and CINTVCC near the IC between INTVCC and power ground.
